name: Tour

examples.title: Basic Tour
examples.code:
function example() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const filtersRef = React.useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null);
  const exportRef = React.useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null);

  return (
    <>
      <Buttons>
        <Button ref={filtersRef}>Filters</Button>
        <Button ref={exportRef}>Export</Button>
        <Button color="primary" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>
          Take the tour
        </Button>
      </Buttons>
      <Tour open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
        <Tour.Step title="Welcome">
          A quick look around the list and its tools.
        </Tour.Step>
        <Tour.Step target={filtersRef} title="Filters">
          The Filters button narrows the list by status and owner.
        </Tour.Step>
        <Tour.Step target={exportRef} title="Export" position="left">
          The Export button downloads the rows you see as a CSV file.
        </Tour.Step>
      </Tour>
    </>
  );
}

accessibility:
There's no WAI-ARIA pattern for a tour, so each step is a
[dialog](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/), modal with the overlay and
non-modal without it:

- A step is a `role="dialog"`, named by its title through `aria-labelledby`, or by an `aria-label`
  on the `Tour.Step`, and described by its body. A development build warns about a step with
  neither a title nor a label.
- With the overlay, the step has `aria-modal="true"`, and the page under it is out of reach for
  everyone: everything else on the page is `inert`, the page doesn't scroll, the overlay takes
  every click, and Tab and Shift+Tab stay in the step. The target is out of reach too, so say in
  the step's body what it is: the spotlight tells a screen reader nothing.
- Without the overlay, nothing claims modality. The page and the target stay usable, by pointer
  and keyboard alike: Tab from the step's last control moves focus to the target, to its first
  control or the target itself when it takes focus, and Shift+Tab goes where the browser sends it. Escape ends the tour
  while focus is in the step, so an Escape meant for a field on the page stays with it.
- Opening moves focus to Next, or, on a step without one that takes focus, to the footer's first
  control, else the body's, else the close button. Ending the tour hands focus back to whatever had it when the tour
  opened. On a step change, focus stays on the control used, so Enter on Next keeps going, and
  goes back to where the step starts when that control is gone, as Back is on the first step.
- After each step change, a polite `role="status"` line inside the step says where the tour is,
  "Step 2 of 5: Filters", since a dialog whose name changes isn't announced again.
- <kbd>ArrowRight</kbd> and <kbd>ArrowLeft</kbd> press the step's Next and Back while focus is in
  the step, swapped under right-to-left text, but not from a text field, another control that
  uses the arrows, or a dialog inside the step. A step whose Next or Back is missing, hidden or
  disabled ignores that key, and nothing happens past either end: ArrowRight doesn't finish the
  tour. The key presses the button as a click does, so a Next or Back given `type="submit"`
  submits its form.
- Skip and the close button always end the tour, so a modal step is never a keyboard trap, and
  <kbd>Escape</kbd> does too unless `closeOnEscape={false}`. A Modal or Dialog opened from a step
  takes Escape and Tab until it closes.
- The scroll to a target is the only motion: the spotlight and the step move with the target
  rather than glide after it, and under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the scroll is instant.
- With `mode="beacon"`, the beacons are real `<button>`s with `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and
  `aria-expanded="false"`, in one `role="group"` named "Tips", in step order after the page's
  content. Each is named "Show tip" and its step's title, has a hit area of at least 24 by 24
  pixels, and stops pulsing under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. Showing them moves no focus,
  and closing a beacon's step hands focus back to its beacon.
- In forced colors, the overlay keeps dimming the page, since it's an SVG fill, the spotlight gets
  a `Highlight` outline, and the step keeps its border.

A tour sits at the modal layer, under toasts. In a modal step, a popup that renders through a portal
of its own, such as a Popover with `appendToBody` or a picker's calendar, renders inside the step,
as it does in a Modal, so it shows over the tour and stays reachable. A `ConfigProvider`'s
`portalContainer` still comes first, there as in a Modal. A step without the overlay
leaves it in `<body>`, under the tour, so keep such content in place inside a non-modal step.
summary: The `Tour` component walks a user through an interface one step at a time, each step a panel pointing at an element with the rest of the page dimmed around it. Each step is a dialog. With the overlay, the default, it's modal: the page under it is inert and still, Tab stays in the step and Escape ends the tour. Without it, the step is a non-modal dialog and the page stays usable.

props.name: children
props.description: `Tour.Step`s, in the order the tour visits them. Fragments are opened up, and anything that isn't a `Tour.Step`, a component that renders one included, is left out.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether it shows from the start (uncontrolled). A tour has to measure its targets, so it shows from the commit after hydration, never in server markup.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with `false` when the tour ends: Skip, the close button, Escape, a click outside with `closeOnClickOutside`, or Done after `onFinish`. With `mode="beacon"` it never fires: those close only the open step, and the app owns `open`.

props.name: value
props.description: The current step's index (controlled). In guided mode an index past either end shows the nearest step, and a fraction is rounded down. With `mode="beacon"`, the open step's index, or `-1` while only the beacons show, as Timeline's `active` takes `-1` for none.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The step it starts on (uncontrolled), and goes back to each time it opens.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the new index when Back, Next, an arrow key or a beacon changes the step, and with `-1` when a beacon's step closes: Done, Escape, the close button, a press outside with `closeOnClickOutside`, or its step being removed, or moved by a step added or removed before it. So keep a beacon tour's list of steps fixed while a tip shows, and drop read ones the next time the tips open.

props.name: onFinish
props.description: Called when Done on the last step finishes the tour, before `onOpenChange(false)`. Skip, the close button, Escape and a click outside don't call it, and with `mode="beacon"`, where Done closes only the step, it never fires.

props.name: overlay
props.description: Dims the page and makes each step modal: `aria-modal`, the rest of the page inert and still, and Tab held in the step. With `false`, a step is a non-modal dialog, as a `Popover` is, and the page and its target stay usable, from the keyboard too: focus moves in and back, Tab from the step's last control, Next in the default footer, goes on to the target (its first control, or the target itself when it takes focus), Shift+Tab goes where the browser sends it, and Escape ends the tour while focus is in the step. A `Tour.Step` can set its own, and a step that turns modal while focus is out on the page takes focus.

props.name: closeOnEscape
props.description: Ends the tour on Escape, or with `mode="beacon"` closes the open step. With the overlay, from anywhere, while no overlay opened over it, such as a Modal opened from a step, is on top. Without it, only while focus is in the step, so an Escape meant for the page stays with the page. A popup inside the step, and content that calls `preventDefault()` on the key, take it first.

props.name: closeOnClickOutside
props.description: Ends the tour on a press outside the step, the overlay included. Content the step renders through a portal counts as inside. Off by default, unlike Popover's: a tour is a sequence someone means to finish, and a stray click on the dimmed page, or on the page around a step without the overlay, shouldn't end it partway. Skip, the close button and Escape still end it. With `mode="beacon"`, a press outside closes the open step, as Escape does, and never ends the tour, and it's off there by default too, so with the default it does nothing.

props.name: portal
props.description: Where the tour renders: `true` for the `ConfigProvider` portal container or `<body>`, a selector or an element for another container, `false` for where it's written. Modal's shape, with a different default. The step and the overlay are fixed to the viewport wherever they render, so a `transform` on an ancestor of an in-place tour moves them with it.

props.name: titleAs
props.description: What every step's title renders as: a heading one level under the heading the tour's page sits beneath, or `p`.

props.name: footer
props.description: Every step's footer, in place of the default: Skip and the progress line at the start, Back and Next at the end. Build it from `Tour.Skip`, `Tour.Back`, `Tour.Next` and `Tour.Progress`, which act on the tour from wherever they sit in the step. ArrowRight and ArrowLeft press the step's `Tour.Next` and `Tour.Back`, swapped under right-to-left text, so one that's disabled, loading or `aria-disabled`, or whose `onClick` prevents, holds for the keys too, and a step without one ignores its key. A step's own `footer` wins, and `null` leaves the steps without one.

props.name: mode
props.description: `guided` walks the steps in order. `beacon` puts a button on each target that opens its step, in any order, and keeps the buttons there until `open` turns `false`. The beacons sit in one group named by `labels.beacons`, in step order, after the page's own content in the Tab order, so order the steps as the page reads; a development build warns once when they aren't. A beacon sits over its target's top end corner and shows while its target is on the page, has a box and is in view, that corner included. Opening one hides them all and opens its step, modal or not by `overlay`, and closing the step brings them back, with focus on its beacon while the step held it. A beacon's step has no Skip, Back or progress line, its Next reads Done and closes the step, and the arrow keys do nothing in it. Closing the tour while its step holds focus sends focus to the step's target. Removing a step removes its beacon, so an app can drop the tips a user has read; a tip whose step is removed or moved while it's open closes, with `onChange(-1)`. While only the beacons show, the tour sits under the app's navbar, sidebars, modals and dropdown menus; raise `--bulma-tour-beacon-z-index` for targets inside one.

parts.catchAll: All standard <div> attributes and Bulma helper props

parts.summary: One step of the tour: a title, a body and the element it points at. It renders nothing where it's written.

props.name: target
props.description: The element the step points at. Without one, or while it isn't on the page or has no box (in a closed Collapse or a hidden tab panel), the step is centered. A target that turns up later, or gets a box, is found then. A development build warns about a missing target, once for each selector.

props.name: title
props.description: The title, which names the step's dialog. A step without one needs an `aria-label`, and a development build warns when it has neither.

props.name: children
props.description: The body, which describes the step's dialog. Say what the target is: a modal step leaves it out of reach, and the spotlight says nothing to a screen reader.

props.name: position
props.description: The side of the target the panel sits on. It flips to the opposite side when it doesn't fit, or to a side across when neither does, as beside a target on a phone, and stays inside the viewport.

props.name: overlay
props.description: This step's own `overlay`, in place of the tour's.

props.name: cover
props.description: Media above the header, such as an image or a short clip, which fills the step's width. Give an image the `alt` it needs, which is `""` when the body already says what it shows, and don't autoplay motion when the user asks for less of it.

props.name: footer
props.description: This step's footer, in place of the tour's `footer` or the default one. `null` leaves the step without one.

parts.catchAll: All standard <div> attributes and Bulma helper props

parts.summary: A `Button` that ends the tour early, labelled `labels.skip` unless it has children. It renders nothing on a beacon's step.

props.name: color
props.description: Bulma color variant for the button. `ghost` renders a link-like button; `text` renders a minimal text-only button.

props.name: isLight
props.description: Applies the light variant of a colored button, such as `primary`'s. Bulma gives the grayscale colors none, so with no `color`, or with `white` or `black`, `isLight` gives the light button, as `color="light"` does, and `light` or `dark` with `isLight` looks the same as without it.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Displays a loading spinner, with everything inside the button hidden behind it, in forced colors (Windows' contrast themes) too. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the spinner stops and stays drawn. It keeps focus, and shows Bulma's focus outline while it has it from the keyboard. Bulma alone hides only the label and draws no focus ring on a loading button, so the rest needs bestax's CSS loaded.

props.name: isFullWidth
props.deprecationNote: Use `isFullwidth` instead — `isFullwidth` wins if both are set.

props.name: isOutlined
props.description: Applies outlined styling (requires color). On the dark scheme, bestax's stylesheets draw the label and border at the lightness Bulma picks for the color's text on the page wherever that's lighter, so a dark color reads there. On a surface that stays light on both schemes, give the surface Bulma's `theme-light` class (with the class prefix in a prefixed build), which keeps what's inside it on the light scheme's values.

props.name: isActive
props.description: Applies active styling (visual only), with no `aria-pressed`. For a button that stays pressed, use `ToggleButton`.

extraProps.name: type
extraProps.description: Button type. Defaults to `'button'`, so a part inside a form doesn't submit it. The arrow keys press Next and Back as a click does, so one given `'submit'` submits its form on an arrow key too.

extraProps.name: onClick
extraProps.description: Runs before the part acts on the tour. Call `preventDefault()` to keep it from acting.
